[{"sha":"a0139cf6a7ad72a685420f53479a99fe385cf394","node_id":"C_kwDOAPKd99oAKGEwMTM5Y2Y2YTdhZDcyYTY4NTQyMGY1MzQ3OWE5OWZlMzg1Y2YzOTQ","commit":{"author":{"name":"Patrik Simek (bot)","email":"bot@patriksimek.cz","date":"2026-09-08T16:18:42Z"},"committer":{"name":"Patrik Simek (bot)","email":"bot@patriksimek.cz","date":"2026-09-08T16:18:42Z"},"message":"test: quarantine the five pool-dependent GHSA-489w cases under Bun

Bun has no shared Buffer allocation pool: Buffer.from("hello") owns an
exact-size 5-byte store, where Node hands out a window into a 64 KiB pool.
Four of the GHSA-489w-w794-jq94 cases depend on that pool for their oracle
and stop at their own "test would be vacuous" precondition on JSC; the
fifth (Test 2) reads the intended sharing of an OWNING store -- the same
behaviour its Test 8 control asserts -- as corruption, because on JSC that
buffer is never pooled. None is a defence gap: the bounding in
lib/bridge.js is only reachable for a non-owning view, and no pool exists
on Bun to leak.

Registered as phase-2, security: false entries in test/bun-skips.js. Full
suite under Bun 1.4.0: 984 planned, 921 executed, 0 failing, completeness
checker green; engine-selftest confirms each entry hits exactly one title.
